A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ESPFormer and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Retained content can be matched across formatting changes, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, sentiment-analysis, translation, and runtime experiments, including ESPFormer results and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds TweetEval evaluation, sorting-mode comparisons, and slicer ablations.

M1.justification: V2 adds temperature-annealed fine-tuning followed by replacement of soft sorting with hard sorting at inference (Section 4.4). This changes the training and inference procedure and introduces an exact-permutation variant; the original soft-sorting pipeline in Algorithm 1 remains.

E1.justification: V2 adds TweetEval sentiment classification, extending sentiment evaluation from movie reviews to tweets. All previous datasets and tasks remain; the MNIST patch-size experiment moves to Appendix A.2.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators remain Transformer, DiffTransformer, and Sinkformer, including on TweetEval. Changed Sinkhorn iteration counts concern experimental settings, while sorting and slicer variants are internal ablations.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 40-epoch annealing protocol and separate sharpened-soft and hard-sort evaluations across the existing Cats and Dogs data fractions. It also introduces a slicer experiment varying L over 1, 8, 32, 64, and 128 and inverse temperature over 0.1, 1, and 10. Runtime comparisons replace Sinkformer S=50 with S=3. Existing task-training schedules remain documented unchanged.

E4.justification: New comparisons test the effects of annealing and hard-sort inference (Table 1), and whether learnable, frozen, or axis-aligned slicing performs better as slice count and inverse temperature vary (Table 6). These substantially expand evidence about core design choices. The previous data-scarcity and MNIST patch-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Retained experiments preserve their run counts and reporting practices: three-run means and standard deviations for Cats and Dogs, four-run ModelNet40 and translation summaries, and ten-run runtime averages. New ablations extend the existing mean-and-standard-deviation practice without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or an explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds TweetEval, slicer-grid, and hard-sort runtime results. Its expanded Cats and Dogs table reports 80.61% sharpened-soft and 81.23% hard-sort accuracy at full data after additional fine-tuning, alongside the retained 79.47% initial result; these are different training conditions. IMDb Sinkformer median accuracy changes from 85.40% to 85.39%, and Transformer worst accuracy from 85.30% to 85.20%. ModelNet40, translation, and MNIST results remain.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Equation 4 by adding the missing 1/p power, writes the transport map with F_mu(x), and specifies absolute continuity rather than continuity. It also introduces the mathematical observation that lower-triangular doubly-stochastic attention reduces to the identity. The main ESP construction remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a substantive contribution: annealed fine-tuning followed by hard-sort inference is claimed to produce exact doubly-stochastic matrices, reduce complexity from O(N^2) to O(LN log N), and improve Cats and Dogs accuracy. This extends the original efficiency contribution beyond parallel soft sorting; the other principal claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes approximate double stochasticity during soft-sort training from exact hard-sort inference. It adds limitations concerning strictly causal/autoregressive attention and memory growth with slice count, interprets the slicer ablation, and qualifies the soft-sort runtime advantage to Sinkformer with S>3. These materially clarify applicability and efficiency.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 supplies an implementation repository address. V2 documents the 40-epoch annealing schedule, decay factor 0.8, and TweetEval implementation and hyperparameters. Most previous implementation details and appendix hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to TweetEval and Constrained Sliced Wasserstein Embedding, the latter supporting discussion of learned slicing. The broader positioning relative to Sinkformer, ESP, soft sorting, and differential attention remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition is retained, with localized wording and terminology clarifications. V2 introduces sorting and slicer subsections, adds Limitations and Impact Statement sections, and moves the MNIST discussion into Appendix A.2. The overall introduction–background–method–experiments structure remains.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. V2 restructures the Cats and Dogs table into baseline and sorting-mode groups, adds TweetEval and slicer tables, revises runtime plots and legends, and relocates the MNIST figure. Existing figures, tables, and the algorithm are extensively resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central attention design through sorting-mode and slicer ablations, clarifies approximate versus exact double stochasticity, and documents important causal and memory limitations absent from v1. Code-access information further improves reproducibility. The extra 40 fine-tuning epochs limit comparisons with unchanged baselines, and broad efficiency wording remains in the conclusion and Appendix A, but the additional design evidence and clearer applicability address important weaknesses in v1.
